t.1.135.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: A certain friend of Vidura, a skilled digger, spoke these words to the Pāṇḍavas somewhere in a secluded place, O king.
t.1.135.2: I am a highly skilled digger, sent by Vidura with the charge, "What is dear to the Pāṇḍavas must be done." What shall I do for you?
t.1.135.4: On the fourteenth night of the dark fortnight, Purocana will set fire to the door of this house of yours.
t.1.135.3: Vidura secretly told me, “Bring about the welfare of the Pāṇḍavas here, as one they can trust.” What shall I do for you?
t.1.135.5: "The Pāṇḍavas, bulls among men, are to be burned together with their mother": this, O Pārtha, I have heard is the resolve of Dhārtarāṣṭra.
t.1.135.7: Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī, steadfast in truth, said to him: "I recognize you, gentle one, as indeed a friend of Vidura."
t.1.135.6: Something was said to you by Vidura in the language of the Mlecchas, O Pāṇḍava, and you answered, “So be it.” Let this be the ground for your trust in me.
t.1.135.8: Toward one who is pure, trustworthy, dear, and ever firmly devoted, a wise man has no need of any token of recognition.
t.1.135.10: It is my belief that this dwelling is made to burn, built for my sake by Purocana at the command of Dhārtarāṣṭra.
t.1.135.9: As he is ours, so are you ours; we make no distinction where you are concerned. We are yours just as we are his; protect us as the wise one would.
t.1.135.11: That evil one, wicked-minded, possesses a treasury and has allies as well; and that corrupt-souled man constantly oppresses us too.
t.1.135.12: So may you, sir, strive to free us from this fire, for if we were burned here, Suyodhana would have his desire fulfilled.
t.1.135.13: This well-stocked armory belongs to that evil-minded one; built right up against the rampart, this great structure has been made so that there is no remedy against it.
t.1.135.15: This is that very calamity which the Kṣattṛ foresaw long ago, and now it has come upon us. You must set us free, unknown to Purocana.
t.1.135.14: This, surely, is that inauspicious deed which he intends to do. Vidura knew of it beforehand, and therefore he warned us.
t.1.135.17: And in the middle of that house he made an opening, not very large, fitted with a door, unknown to others and level with the ground, O Bhārata.
t.1.135.16: Promising, "So be it," the digger set to work with great diligence, and, under the pretext of clearing out the moat, he made a very large tunnel.
t.1.135.19: There, O king, all the sons of Pāṇḍu dwelt through the night with their weapons at hand, and by day they roamed from forest to forest, hunting.
t.1.135.18: Out of fear of Purocana, he kept the mouth of the tunnel concealed, for that evil-minded man always dwells there at the door of the house.
t.1.135.20: Distrustful yet acting as though they trusted him, deceiving Purocana, discontented yet seeming content, O king, they dwelt there in the deepest sorrow.
t.1.135.21: And the men who dwelt in the city did not become aware of them, except for that minister of Vidura, the best of diggers.
